boards.printed: The kit name LP-MSPM0L1306 and its revision (for example Rev. A) are printed sideways on the right half of the board, between the TEXAS INSTRUMENTS logo and the S2 button (TI's board drawing, SLAU869E; mspm0l1306/img/board-tour.png).

recovery.saves: the main flash and both configuration areas, as three .bin files in your Downloads folder (cc2755p10-<time>-main.bin, -ccfg.bin, -scfg.bin), and only if the board holds a different program
recovery.changes: erases the main flash (TI's security firmware at the top stays) and rewrites both configuration areas, CCFG and SCFG
recovery.back: This page cannot put those files back. TI's UniFlash can, with the repository's restore script.
recovery.tool: TI UniFlash 9.6.0 (its DSLite command line) on a Mac
files: SCFG, 1 kB at 0x4E040000; the script checks its CRC32
steps: Put the three files in one folder and rename them as in the table.
In a copy of this repository, with UniFlash installed at /Applications/ti/uniflash_9.6.0, run: cc2755p10/restore.sh <that folder>
It erases the chip (keeping TI's security firmware), writes all three, reads the main flash and CCFG back, and prints RESTORED when they match.
recovery.tested: Not tested with files this page saved. The same steps worked on 2026-10-09 with files read by TI's DSLite.

boards.note: Recognized. This page puts small programs on it (blink, a console message, the buttons, a Zigbee light, a Bluetooth light), reads its console and puts back what was on it.

recovery.saves: the main flash and the configuration area, as two .bin files in your Downloads folder (cc2340r5-<time>-main.bin and -ccfg.bin), and only if the board holds a different program that starts; a board with no program has nothing to save
recovery.changes: erases the main flash and rewrites the configuration area (CCFG)
recovery.back: This page cannot put those files back. TI's UniFlash can, with the repository's put-back script.
recovery.tool: TI UniFlash 9.6.0 (its DSLite command line) on a Mac
steps: Put the two files from one save in a folder of their own.
In a copy of this repository, with UniFlash installed at /Applications/ti/uniflash_9.6.0 and your probe's serial in cc2340r5/CC2340R5.ccxml, run: cc2340r5/restore-from-page.sh <that folder>

It merges the two files, erases the chip, writes them, reads main flash and CCFG back and prints RESTORED when they match. A program that keeps data in TI's NVS area (the top 4 kB; a Zigbee image keeps its network there) may write it as soon as it starts; the script reports those bytes rather than failing.
recovery.tested: Passed on 2026-10-16 with files this page saved: a Zigbee alarm image went back read-back identical (except 375 bytes it wrote to its own NVS area after starting) and answered Home Assistant without being paired again; the put-back took 30 s.

console.port: the second serial port of the XDS110 (on a Mac /dev/cu.usbmodem<probe serial>1)
console.baudNote: TI's SDK examples print at 115200; the Wi-Fi CSI program prints at 921600

toolbox.command: ./simplelink-wifi-toolbox programmer -i XDS110 -param1 <probe serial> programming --tool_settings <absolute path to tool_settings.json>
toolbox.before: Build and sign the images first: the SDK's make, then the Toolbox image builder, which writes tool_settings.json (cc35x1/README.md steps 1 to 4). The board needs a debugger under it (LP-XDS110ET or LP-XDS110, TGT VDD on EXT) and a second USB-C cable for power.
toolbox.after: The Toolbox does not reset the board: press S1 or run xds110reset -s <probe serial>.
toolbox.note: This page does not write this board. Run the command on your computer.
